full_judgment:
3. Facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of both the revisional proceedings, in short, are that respondent No. 2 Salahuddin Ahmed lodged, a complaint petition, registered as Complaint Petition Case No. 3795 of 2003, before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka alleging that he was a reputed businessman having many business establishments. He was the proprietor of S.A. Paribahan and had business office in almost every district of the country. He was traveling by road on 22-12-2001 to go to his business offices at Sreemongal, Moulavi Bazar and Sylhet with a view to settling annual accounts, paying various debts and renovating his aforesaid business offices and for the said purpose he was carrying with him a sum of take 20 lacs in cash. In the course of journey when he reached at a place near Madhabpur Police station under Habigonj district at 8-00 pm he was advised by an Army officer, then carrying out Clean Heart Operation duty, to go to Madhabpur Police station and make a GD entry about his carrying with him such sum of money in the interest of his safety, security and protection. Accordingly, he went to the Madhabpur Police Station for making a GD entry. The officer-in-charge of the Police station, while making the GD entry, contacted accused petitioner Mostafa Kemal, Superintendent of Police, Habigonj and informed him of the matter. Accused petitioner Mostafa Kamal asked the officer-in-charge of the police station not to allow the complainant respondent Salahuddin Ahmed to resume his journey to Sreemongal and Sylhet and to put him in the than lockup showing him arrested which was done. Accused petitioner Mostafa Kamal made a proposal to him as a part of bargain to pay him a sum of taka 50 lacs including the amount of 20 lacs which was then lying with the complainant and taken away by the police at the police station. Complainant refused to concede to the said proposal. As a result, accused petitioner Superintendent of Police in collusion with accused petitioner Abdul Wahed implicated the complainant respondent in a number of false Crl. cases. In addition thereto, accused petitioner Mostafa Kemal also put him under detention tinder the Special Powers Act, 1971. The complainant was eventually released from the said criminal cases including the said detention case through legal battle in courts. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate examined him on oath and by his order dated 01-12-2003 sent the case for a judicial inquiry to the Metropolitan Magistrate Md. Sujayat Ullah. Accordingly, he held judicial inquiry by examining 4 witnesses including the complainant on 30-12-2003 and 4-01-2004. He returned the case record to the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 15-01-2004 reporting that allegations under sections 220/166/167/161/500 and 501 of the Penal Code were prima facie proved against both the accused petitioners and that the offenders being public servants the offences were triable by Special Judge. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate transmitted the record of the case along with judicial inquiry report to the learned Metro. Sessions Judge, Dhaka who registered it as Metro Special Case No. 39 of 2004. Thereafter, on hearing the learned advocate for the complainant and on perusal of the materials on record he took cognizance of the offence against the accused petitioners for the offence punishable under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. Metropolitan Sessions Judge, (ex-officio Metro. Senior Special Judge), Dhaka wrote a letter on 4-03-2004 to the Government followed by another letter dated 09-03-2004 for sanction but the office of the Prime Minister by its memo dated 22-04-2004 addressed to the Metro. Sessions Judge, declined to accord any sanction for prosecution of the accused petitioners. A copy of the letter was also sent to the Director General, Bureau of Anti Corruption. It was found from the said letter that the sanction was withheld by memo dated 10-04-2004 issued by the Bureau of Anti Corruption. In such a situation the complainant filed another application before the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge with a prayer for sending another letter to the office of Prime Minister seeking sanction for prosecution of the accused petitioners but the learned Metro. Sessions Judge vide his order dated 09-05-2004 refused the said prayer without assigning any reason. The complainant then demanding justice caused a notice dated 28-07-2004 served on the office of the Prime Minister for necessary sanction but without' any success. So, he invoked the writ jurisdiction for the High Court Division. A writ petition was filed which was registered as Writ Petition No. 4256 of 2004 High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 23-03-2005 made the rule absolute asking the Metropolitan Sessions Judge to proceed with the said complaint petition without sanction of the Government in view of the provision of section 28 of the Anti Corruption Commission Act, 2004. Both the accused petitioners and Government preferred Civil Appeal Nos. 139 and 140 of 2006 before the Ho'nble Appellate Division. Their Lordships by their judgment and order dated 23-08-2009 dismissed the said appeals. (It deserves mention here that the accused petitioners preferred Civil Review Petition No. 113 of 2010 seeking review of the judgment and order of dismissal passed in Civil Appeal No. 139 of 2006 but the same was dismissed for non-prosecution on 03-07-2012). Subsequent events show that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka by his order dated 23-11-2009 transferred the record of Metro Special case No. 39 of 2004 to the Special Judge, Court No. 3 Dhaka for trial. It was registered as Special Case No. 01 of 2010. The petitioners then moved separate applications for their discharge under section 241 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which the learned Special Judge by his order dated 21-03-2010 refused and by his order dated 04-04-2010 framed Charge against the accused petitioner Mostafa Kamal for the offence punishable under sections 409/161 and 167 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947 and against the accused petitioner Wahed Miah for the offence punishable under sections 161 and 167 of the Penal Code read with aforesaid section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, such offence being committed by them between 22-12-2002 and 02-01-2003 (both the dates are inclusive). 

 4. Being aggrieved by the charges dated 04-04-2004 framed against them the accused petitioners preferred Crl. Rev. No. 687 and 688 of 2010 under section 439 read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 25-04-2010 which were, however, rejected as being not pressed by them. Accused petitioner Mostafa Kamal then preferred Crl. Misc. Case No. 19998 of 2010 under section 561A of the Code of criminal Procedure while accused petitioner Wahed Miah preferred Crl. Misc. Case No. 23869 of 2010 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Stay was also granted therein. At this, the complainant moved a Crl. Misc. Petition No. 371 of 2010, thereafter Crl. Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 408 of 2010 which the  Appellate Division disposed of with a direction upon Mr. Justice Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah of the High Court Division (then as he was) to dispose of the said rule within 11-01-2011. The Division Bench presided over by his Lordship heard the Rule in connection with the said Crl. Misc. Case No. 19998 of 2010 and discharged the same with an observation that the accused petitioner might proceed under section 10 (1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and might raise a point of grievance in respect of the charge framed against him under section 409 of the Penal Code. Accordingly, accused petitioner Mostafa Kamal preferred the instant Crl. Revision No. 256 of 2011. On the other hand, on the application of accused petitioner Wahed Miah this Bench converted his proceedings of Crl. Misc. Case No. 23869 of 2010 under section 561A of The Code of Criminal Procedure into one of Revision under section 10(1A) of the Crl. Law Amendment Act, 1958, being Crl. Revision No. 1483 of 2012. 

 7. Mr. M. Amir UI Islam appearing with Mr. Mahbubur Rahman, both senior advocates, has submitted that there was hardly any occasion to decide the materials and evidence on record in order to seek justification for the charge framed against the accused petitioner Mostafa Kamal under sections 409 of the Penal Code and against both of them under sections 161 and 167 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Preventions of Corruption Act, 1947. He has further drawn our attention to a decision in the case' of S.A. Satter-Vs-State and others, reported in 14 BLD (AD) 1994 at page-36 and has submitted that the purpose of examination under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is to see whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding and not to see whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding and not to see whether there is sufficient ground for conviction. Mr. Md. Moniruzzaman Rubel, learned Deputy Attorney General, has adopted the submission's made by Mr. M. Amirul Islam. In this connection we have also perused the decisions in the case of Syed Ahmed and another-Vs-Habibur Rahman reported in 42 DLR (1990) HCD at page-240, Chandra das Singh-Vs- Prokash Chandra Bose and another reported in AIR 1963 (SC)1430, Badsha Mia and others-Vs-The state reported in 10 DLR(1958) HCD-412, and Suresh Chandra Vadilal Shah-Vs-Shantilal Shankartlal and another reported in 1968 Cr.LJ-117 cited by the learned advocate for the accused petitioners regarding the purpose of holding judicial inquiry. We do not disown the fact that the purpose of judicial inquiry is to ascertain truth or falsehood of the allegation. But it does not appear to us that purpose of such inquiry is to ascertains if the allegations, prima facie made out, would end in conviction. We do not find any potent ground to hold that charge could not be framed beyond the citation of sections of offence mentioned at the heading of the complaint petition even if the contents of the complaint petition and the result of judicial inquiry (based on such complaint) made out case of offence under different other sections of law. 

 11. Order of stay passed in Crl. Misc. Case No. 23869 of 2010 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (later converted into Crl. Revision No. 1483 of 2012 under section 10(1 A) of the Criminal Law amendment Act, 1958) is hereby vacated.
